capability.summary: Project an input CSV to named columns and return the resulting CSV text inside JSON
capability.description: Reads one CSV file with pandas defaults, splits the required `columns_to_filter` string on commas, trims and drops empty tokens, verifies every resulting column name exists, and returns the selected columns in their requested order as in-memory CSV text. It does not write an output file or filter rows.
capability.problem_space: Exact-name column projection from one local CSV into returned CSV text; not row filtering, data cleansing, aggregation, format conversion to structured JSON rows, or persistent file rewriting.

constraint.io_signature: Input: one required CSV file path plus required columns_to_filter: string containing exact column names separated by commas (for example `name,email,age`); output: JSON containing selected-column CSV text and metadata or a precise error.
accepted_inputs: an existing CSV file readable by pandas.read_csv with default options
one comma-separated string of exact column names, such as `name,email,age`; the script applies split(',') and trims each token
constraint.output_shape: Success: {status: "success", tool: "pandas", target: string, kept_columns: string[], row_count: integer, csv: string}; csv includes a header and all input rows for only the requested columns. Missing requested columns: {status: "error", tool: "pandas", message: string, available: string[]} and exit 1. Read/parse/serialization exception: {status: "error", tool: "pandas", message: string} and exit 1. Missing file: {status: "error", message: string} and exit 2. Fewer than two arguments prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: filters columns only and never filters rows, evaluates predicates, aggregates values, or modifies the source file
uses pandas.read_csv defaults with no delimiter, encoding, dtype, quoting, header, NA, or chunking options
loads the entire CSV and generated output into memory and applies no timeout or output truncation
column matching is exact after trimming comma-separated tokens; an empty effective list is allowed and produces a zero-column CSV representation

input_contract.name: columns_to_filter
input_contract.description: Comma-separated exact column names; the script splits this single string on commas, trims tokens, and ignores empty tokens.

output_contract.description: JSON transport envelope containing selected column names, row count, and the projected dataset as an embedded CSV string, or explicit read/column errors.

semantic_output.description: On a success envelope, the csv field is the projected CSV artifact consumed by downstream steps and produced_files aliases.

intent_tags: keep selected columns from a CSV file
return a CSV column projection as text in JSON
negative_intents: filter CSV rows by values or conditions
write a filtered CSV file to disk
convert CSV rows into a JSON array or perform analytics
